title: Exactly what I expected
text:
My Kenmore refrigerator had been having problems with not activating cooling consistently. I determined it to be thermostat based on how cooling wouldn't start, but I could make it run by giving my fridge a whack right by the temp controls. I found the part and instructions on how to replace it on the sears parts direct site. Not wanting to pay almost $80 for the part if I didn't need to, I searched for the part number listed on Amazon and found this item for under $15 - that is a hefty price difference and since the reviews were generally good, I went ahead and purchased it. It got to me in under 2 days and took about 15 minutes to install.

I will say the insulating sleeve on it seems to be a little cheap (not even sure it is intended to be for insulating). I tried to swap it for the original one, but the end of the sensor is a little thicker then the original insulating sleeve will allow. I assume this will mean that I need to set my fridge to be a little colder than I had before.

Very happy with this replacement part for the price.

Only time will tell how well this is manufactured, but at the price, getting 2 years use out of it will make it more than worth it considering that my fridge is only 9 years old.

title: Powerful, looks great, easy to clean
text:
This range is great. It's super powerful, I used the center burner for the first time the other day and it cooked things in the wok perfectly (and fast!). I like that there are different sized burners. I usually cook for one, and a small pot will boil over on simmer on all but the smallest burner. Just move it to that one if you're having issues with it being too hot.

It looks great, the grates are nice quality and flat, plus they sort of lock onto the bottom so they're all lined up nicely. I like that underneath the burners is all one surface, so you're not scooping out around each burner all the time to clean it. Simply take the grates off and you can wipe the entire bottom down if you want to, including swiping pieces off the side to be able to get them out.

There are 2 annoying things. First that the ignition continues for a long time after the flame is on, it takes some getting used to to operate the knobs..also that it won't go past high if you're still pushing on the knob. I'm used to it after a few weeks now though.

The other thing is the surface the knobs are on looks dirty if you wipe it with a sponge, you have to get a cloth or paper towel to clean it. I didn't realize that the knobs had so many indentations either, those are not the easiest to clean.

I had it professionally installed, so I don't know how easy it was.

title: I would recommend saving some money and going with this one.
text:
I just installed this Waterdrop Water Filter in our Samsung refrigerator and it worked great! Our refrigerator "filter" light came on, letting me know that it was time to replace it. I looked it up on Amazon, and there was both the genuine Samsung part, and the compatible generic part. Sometimes I'm wary of the generic ones because they may not necessarily use all the same filtering material as the OEM, but this was at a lower price, and who doesn't like saving money? I've used another generic filter for our fridge before, and it worked great too. This time I had the opportunity to try this one, so I went for it. I ordered this one, and it came quickly with instructions on how to replace the old one with it. It was really simple, basically just taking the old one out of its little hole in the bottom of the refrigerator section and putting this one in its place. You have to run the water a bit after you first install it because it comes out a little wild at first, but that's true with any new filter. We've been using it for a couple days now, it seems to work great, I can't tell the difference between this one and the old original Samsung filter. I will update if anything changes, but I would recommend saving some money and going with this one.

title: The lil warsher that could, did and then dosent
text:
It arrived quickly was easy to set up so within days of ordering I began putting this small wonder to the test. I ran every cycle, did different types of loads, and it leaked, it leaked every run, no matter how much water was in it. Undaunted, I mopped up after it and continued. My clothes came out clean, fresh and were spun so well it only took them a half day to dry hung indoors. Then I did a load of sweaters, the lint trap filled up, I cleared it and followed it with blankets and that was it, it choked. Unable to drain I could hear the motor running but the tub wouldnt clear. So i emptied it, unhooked the tubes underneath and let it drain that way. Darn it. I contacted Panda and they said “junk it we’ll replace it”. Impressive. OK of they are willing to stand by their product Im willing to give it another try. A little wiser this time. The “new” one has yet to leak. Cut to less than six months later tge second one is dead. First off I thought it was great that they sent me another one, but it was used. The tub had a cut in it and the motor was broke from its base but I figured if it ran, “whatever”.
These machines are great when they run, they run well. The clothes come out clean and nearly dry. But the water pumps are tiny and clearly too small. I dont think its worth $275 which is about what I paid for it.
PS. They sent me a new/refurbished water pump. I spliced it in after I couldnt get the wires to pull out. And its running again. Now Im trying to run loads 6L and under and have asked my roomie bot to run the spun cycle repeatedly since its not Necessary and it engages the water pump. I’m hoping if I take it easy on the water pump the rest will hold up. Fingers Crossed! I also found some water pumps for it online and pump them away for backup. Had to order from China took 3wks to arrive.

It's a pretty great little machine. I'd have appreciated something telling me where to pour the water, since there's nothing showing you and if this is the first ice maker you have used, it's not really clear where it goes. Spoiler alert, pour it in the same side as the basket.

It's fairly quiet. Not whisper quiet, and I wouldn't try to sleep next to it, but it hasn't disturbed me while I've been doing other stuff.

title: Less expensive than OEM but I am leery of the quality
text: When your dishwasher starts leaking water, you gotta get it fixed. The OEM Whirlpool item was triple the price and a week+ for delivery, so I went with this cheaper model with 1-day delivery through Amazon. Installation was pretty straight forward if your have any DIY/handyman skills.  But it seems like our dishwasher is louder now, in that we hear a more pronounced water swishing and washing - I don't know if its a coincidence, or we're just more aware of it, or if this diverter valve and motor don't quite line up like the original. But it works. Time will tell how long it lasts (it was not as well built/sturdy as the OEM that seems to use thicker plastic). Additionally, when installing the rubber grommet, it felt loose when fitted in place, so I took it back out, put a thin bead of silicone sealant around the outside edge, fitted it back in place and let it sit overnight to dry. The next day I finished the installation and it has not leaked.  Looking back, I probably could have just replaced that grommet to fix the leak, but I couldn't be sure if the grommet was leaking or if water was leaking through the water diverter motor, so I replaced both so that I wouldn't have to re-do the job.

title: Works well so far after a month!
text:
In my review photos, the blue wheels are originals. As you can see, the blue wheels were flattened out a bit, apparently, causing the drum so sag just enough to wobble.

The replacement red wheels are nice that they already have the shaft on them. The washer was a bit small so used the larger washer from the original blue wheels.

The new wheels firmed the drum up and works great now. Only needed to replace the two rear drum wheels on our LG dryer

Some advice - Give yourself 2 or 3 hours for this job, and take photos of the different screws you remove, next to where they go, using your mobile phone so you know where they go.

We had to remove the whole inner back panel of the dryer that the wheels are mounted on so that you can remove the nuts off the original wheels easier. Because the originals are on there impossibly tight and there's no way wedging a wrench behind them like on the service videos would've had any clearance to loosen them let alone be able to get a grip on them.. Also, use a metric socket wrench because we only had wrenches 1/2” (too small) and 9/16” (too big) and ended up using vise-grip pliers and it was very hard to loosen the original wheels nut and the vise grips still was deforming the nut. Use an impact wrench with a metric socket and would be no trouble.

title: Very sturdy & well made hat washer
text:
I have an existing hat washer from another brand. I wanted to get another one so that I could wash 2 caps at the same time. I saw this available via the Vine program. I placed the order and it was delivered within 2 days.

Here's my initial impressions of the new one (black) vs the old one (white)
- The new hat washer is much more robust & sturdy, quality is better than the old one
- The new hat washer comes in 3 parts; the old one with 2 pieces
- Even though it appears that you could wash 2 hats simultaneously with the new hat washer, it's recommended to wash only 1 at a time
- The multiple latch points of the new hat washer secures the hat better than the old one; this greatly reduces the risk of the hat washer unexpectedly opening up in the dishwasher
- The new hat washer is slightly longer than the old one (0.50 inch); this may or may not make a difference when placing it in the dishwasher
- The double-sided instructions that accompany the new hat washer are very clear & helpful; the insert for the old hat washer had a few lines that didn't really say much
- Both hat washers work very well in the dishwasher
- The new hat washer can be used in a washing machine on gentle cycle. I haven't tried it yet, but will do so soon; I would never even attempt to use the old hat washer in a washing machine

Overall, I think this new hat washer is great. It's definitely better than the one I already had. I have more flexibility when it comes to washing hats (washing machine vs dishwasher). And now I can wash 2 hats at the same time.

title: Good fit, but developed holes after 1.5 years (!)
text:
The good: this was a good fit for my LG WM2016CW and I was able to install by myself. The lower half of the door boot still seems to be in good condition. AFAICT, no water has leaked out.

The bad: after 1.5 years, I noticed some deformation near the top, then found a hole. I took apart the machine and found two holes (see attached pics). It looks like the rubber degraded---I see small bits of rubber near the two holes.

Notes: this includes a drain port on the bottom, but no ports on the top (what look like ports in the picture are sealed off). My original door boot never developed holes---I replaced it after 10 years after I noticed lots of bacteria/mold growth around the drain port (partly because I didn't realize how much cleaning was necessary after each wash).

So, this did a decent job of extending the life of my LG washer for an additional 1.5 years. But, it's pretty disappointing that it would degrade so quickly. I might still buy the same one as a replacement since it's inexpensive and I'm used to doing the repair now.

Tip: if you are doing the repair yourself, *do* buy yourself the spring expansion tool. The alternative is to attach zip-ties to both ends of the spring, but having the extra hand available to set the wire in place while holding the spring open is invaluable and saved me a ton of frustration on the 2nd try. The 1st try was pretty painful using on the zip-ties...

text: The whole idea is to have less waste in our landfills. I bought the Keurig coffee machine and all the accessories to have the least impact on the environment. I just wasn't prepared for the amount of time it would take to make a cup of coffee. The paper filters that fit in this reusable k cup are difficult to separate especially with arthritis. You have to discover for yourself the correct level of coffee to add. I bought the handy dandy scoop/funnel that measures 2 tablespoons and gets the coffee into the filter with no spilling of the grounds. But 2 tablespoons was too much coffee & it popped the top of the k cup off, the 1st brew. I think it has to do with the gasket closing on 2 layers of paper filter. It's just a matter of trial and error. The thing is, when I want a cup of coffee? I just want to pop a k cup in and brew a cup of coffee, I don't want to play 1)get the reusable k cup out. 2)try to separate the paper filter from the stack 3)get the coffee from the freezer and fill the filter 4)snap the lid on 5) load it into the machine & brew.  I just want a cup of coffee. Yeah yeah yeah, I COULD set it up the night before.😊 I don't always think that far ahead.

title: WON'T LIVE WITHOUT THIS
text: I live in Las Vegas and drink ice water all day long. I got sick of fighting with ice cube trays. Ice doesn't come out of plastic trays, and the modern version of the metal trays our parents used are so flimsy that they break more easily than the ice they contain. I also got sick of ice in my freezer all solidifying into one massive lump. This ice maker is the perfect answer. I just leave it running around the clock. No, it doesn't keep ice frozen, but when the ice melts, the water goes back in the reservoir and is reprocessed. Several times every day, I go to my machine, and there is always ice waiting without struggling with trays or having to chisel cubes apart. If your kitchen isn't set up to allow a fridge with an ice-maker, this is definitely the next-best option. Of course, with Amazon, you know you're going to get the best, fastest delivery possible.
